notes.text: **Genesis 27:28** — וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְרֹב דָּגָן וְתִירֹשׁ — Isaac asks that God grant Jacob heaven's dew, earth's richness, and an abundance of grain and new wine. The whole os unpacks the four terms of this blessing. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereishit Rabbah 66:3** — דָּבָר אַחֵר, מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם זוֹ מִקְרָא, וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ זוֹ מִשְׁנָה, דָּגָן זוֹ תַּלְמוּד, תִּירֹשׁ זֶה אַגָּדָה — in a further reading the four gifts are Scripture, Mishnah, Talmud and Aggadah. Rav Tzadok keeps the plain sense (physical food) and argues that both readings are one, since food's life-giving power is the Torah within it. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 7** (Rav Tzadok) — the os just before reads the same blessing as holiness in eating, takes דָּגָן וְתִירֹשׁ as bread and wine, and maps them onto the Written and Oral Torah through Zohar III 271b (לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחֲמִי); it adds the sefirotic scheme (dew = Keter, from טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא). *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Vayeshev 13** (Rav Tzadok) — joins R. Acha's אֱלָהוּתָא to the same Midrash (מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, אגדה) and adds that these blessings armed Jacob to subdue the evil inclination. *checked*
**Deuteronomy 32:47** — כִּי לֹא דָבָר רֵק הוּא מִכֶּם כִּי הוּא חַיֵּיכֶם — the Torah is no empty matter for you; it is your very life. *Mafteach: missing*
**Deuteronomy 30:19** — הַחַיִּים וְהַמָּוֶת נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ... וּבָחַרְתָּ בַּחַיִּים — I set life and death before you; choose life. Here 'life' is the Torah itself. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 61b** — וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם חִיּוּתֵנוּ אָנוּ מִתְיָרְאִין, בִּמְקוֹם מִיתָתֵנוּ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה — R. Akiva's parable of the fish: if we are afraid even in the water that keeps us alive, how much more so out of it; Torah is to Israel what water is to fish. *Mafteach: found*

**Deuteronomy 8:3** — כִּי לֹא עַל הַלֶּחֶם לְבַדּוֹ יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם כִּי עַל כָּל מוֹצָא פִי ה' יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם — man does not live by bread alone but by whatever comes from God's mouth. The 'well-known' reading he cites takes it as the divine word inside the bread. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shem MiShmuel, Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah 3:8** (Chassidus) — citing the Arizal's Likutei Torah on the same verse, it says the bread feeds a person only in proportion to the share of God's word that is inside it; this is the 'well-known' reading Rav Tzadok relies on.
שהחיות שבלחם שזן את האדם היא לפי ערך חלקי מוצא פי ה' הנמצא בו

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat 3:5** (Rav Tzadok) — the same chain at length: wheat (חִטָּה = 22) is the root of the Torah's twenty-two letters, which is why grain gives the infant דַּעַת (Berakhot 40a); it adds that the manna too is from the 22 letters, but those of the heart rather than the mind. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Tzav 7** (Rav Tzadok) — again חִטָּה בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא כ״ב for the Written Torah and wine for the Oral Torah (Zohar III 271b), noting that the verse says יַיִן מָסָכְתִּי and not 'my wine', because the Oral Torah is what a person draws out of himself. *checked*
**Proverbs 9:5** — לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי — Wisdom calls: come eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed. *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar III 271b** (Ra'aya Meheimna, Ekev; Sefaria: Zohar, Eikev 1:18) — לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְּלַחְמִי, וְדָא נַהֲמָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּבִכְתָב, וְיֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה — the bread of the verse is the Written Torah and the wine is the Oral Torah. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar III 266b; correct: Zohar III 271b)*
**Genesis 26:30** — וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם מִשְׁתֶּה וַיֹּאכְלוּ וַיִּשְׁתּוּ — Isaac makes a feast for Avimelech's party, and they eat and drink. The feast is called by its drinking. *Mafteach: found*
**Genesis 43:31** — וַיִּתְאַפַּק וַיֹּאמֶר שִׂימוּ לָחֶם — Joseph collects himself and orders, 'Serve the bread': the whole meal is called bread. *Mafteach: found*
**Genesis 43:34** — וַיִּשְׁתּוּ וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ — the brothers drank with Joseph and became merry. The same meal is also named by its drinking. *Mafteach: found*

**Mishnah Challah 1:2** (the end of the passage that opens in 1:1) — וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַדָּגָן אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא מֵהֶן — the Sages hold that a vow against 'grain' covers only the five species, which are also the species liable to challah. The same ruling stands in Mishnah Nedarim 7:2 (Nedarim 55a), which Rav Tzadok cites in Toldot 7. *Mafteach: found*
**Numbers 15:19** — וְהָיָה בַּאֲכָלְכֶם מִלֶּחֶם הָאָרֶץ תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה לַה' — the challah verse calls the produce of the five species 'bread of the land'. *Mafteach: found*

**Ecclesiastes 9:7** — לֵךְ אֱכֹל בְּשִׂמְחָה לַחְמֶךָ וּשְׁתֵה בְלֶב טוֹב יֵינֶךָ — eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart: food is 'bread' and drink is 'wine'. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Ecclesiastes 9:2; correct: Ecclesiastes 9:7)*

**Eruvin 65a** — וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְאֶת מֵימֶיךָ, מָה לֶחֶם שֶׁנִּיקָּח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר אַף מַיִם שֶׁנִּיקָּח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר, וּמַאי נִיהוּ? יַיִן, וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ מַיִם — R. Chanin bar Pappa: the 'water' that, like the bread, is bought with tithe money is wine, so Scripture calls wine 'water'. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Pesachim)*

**Exodus 23:25** — וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְאֶת מֵימֶיךָ — serve God and He will bless your bread and your water. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Exodus 23:5; correct: Exodus 23:25)*

**Ta'anit 6b** — אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מִיטְרָא בַּעְלַהּ דְּאַרְעָא הוּא — rain is the 'husband' of the earth, with Isaiah 55:10 as proof. The printed Hebrew of the os reads ו. (6a), but the statement is on 6b. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Taanit 7a; correct: Taanit 6b)*

**Isaiah 55:10** — כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵרֵד הַגֶּשֶׁם וְהַשֶּׁלֶג מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם... כִּי אִם הִרְוָה אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְהוֹלִידָהּ וְהִצְמִיחָהּ — rain waters the earth and makes it give birth and sprout; the verse the Gemara quotes. *Mafteach: missing*

**Bava Kamma 71b–72a** — הַאי דְּלָא אֲמַרִי לְכוּ בְּאוֹרְתָּא... דְּלָא אֲכַלִי בִּשְׂרָא דְתוֹרָא — Rav Nachman explains that he did not give this answer the night before because he had not yet eaten beef (the words fall at the top of 72a). *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bava Kamma 38a; correct: Bava Kamma 72a)*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Likkutei Torah, Tzav 7:9-14** (Chassidus) — R. Shneur Zalman draws the same conclusion from Rav Nachman's beef and from the infant who calls 'abba' only after tasting grain: the food's root, in God's word, adds strength to a person's wisdom and to his service in Shema, prayer and Torah study. He frames it in Kabbalistic terms (the sparks of Tohu), where Rav Tzadok speaks of the Torah inside the food.
שנמצא מובן מזה שהמאכל מוסיף חיות ג״כ בכח החכמה והשכל של האדם

**Tosafot, Bava Kamma 72a** (s.v. דלא אכלי בשרא דתורא) — שָׁרוּי בְּתַעֲנִית הָיָה — he was fasting. Rashi there instead reads it as 'I had not examined the reasoning'; Rav Tzadok takes Tosafot's literal reading, so that the meal itself is what clears the mind. *Mafteach: missing*

**Eruvin 64a** — אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן... דְּהָא אֲנָא כֹּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא שָׁתֵינָא רְבִיעֵתָא דְּחַמְרָא לָא צִילָא דַּעְתַּאי — Rav Nachman: until I drink a revi'it of wine my mind is not clear. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Re'eh 5** (Rav Tzadok) — the same pairing of Bava Kamma 72a and Eruvin 64a, with Rashi and Tosafot shown to agree: for Rav Nachman, meat and wine were themselves words of Torah, his 'bread of his portion' (לֶחֶם חֻקּוֹ); it adds the halakhic question of when one who knows his craving is the soul's may eat meat. *checked*

notes.anchor: מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית
notes.text: **Liturgy, the Yotzer blessing of the morning Shema** — וּבְטוּבוֹ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית — in His goodness He renews the work of Creation every day, continually. He quotes it without naming it. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 3:3** (Rav Tzadok) — refers back to this os by name (וְנִתְבָּאֵר תּוֹלְדוֹת מַאֲמָר ח) and repeats its chain: מִי שֶׁבָּרָא יוֹם בָּרָא פַּרְנָסָתוֹ, המחדש בטובו, and the daily new halakha of Bereishit Rabbah 49. It adds that the new blessing in each day's food matches the person's renewal in Torah and prayer, and that since Sinai the renewal of halakha is handed to Israel's own souls. *checked*
**Tzidkat HaTzadik 216** (Rav Tzadok) — every day has its own new Torah, because God renews Creation daily through the Torah; food carries life-force to the heart, and the passage cites Rav Nachman's beef (Bava Kamma 71b) and the three Shabbat meals. *checked*

**Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Beshalach, Vayassa 2** (Sefaria: Tractate Vayassa 3:4) — דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ... מִי שֶׁבָּרָא יוֹם, בָּרָא פַרְנָסָתוֹ — He who created the day created its sustenance (also in Tanchuma, Beshalach 20). *Mafteach: missing*
**Exodus 16:4** — וְיָצָא הָעָם וְלָקְטוּ דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ — the people shall gather each day's portion on its day; the verse on which the Mekhilta comments. *Mafteach: missing*

**Bereishit Rabbah 49:2** — אֵין יוֹם וָיוֹם שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ הֲלָכָה בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה — there is no day on which God does not bring forth a new halakha in the heavenly court. *Mafteach: found*

**Job 11:9** — אֲרֻכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּה וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם — its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea. Tanchuma, Noach 3 applies the verse to the Oral Torah, as Rav Tzadok does here. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Torah Ohr, Miketz 11:12** (Chassidus) — the Alter Rebbe also reads Isaac's blessing (מטל השמים זו מקרא ומשמני הארץ זו משנה) through ארוכה מארץ מדה: the Torah's light reaches beyond all measure, and Isaac, the root of measure (gevurah), is the one who passes it to Jacob.
שהברכה היא מטל השמים זו מקרא ומשמני הארץ זו משנה. שעי"ז יומשך תוספת אור יותר לאין שיעור
**Ecclesiastes 7:12** — וְיִתְרוֹן דַּעַת הַחָכְמָה תְּחַיֶּה בְעָלֶיהָ — the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom keeps alive those who have it. *Mafteach: found*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3** — לְפִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ צַעַר גָּדוֹל וְנִדּוּד שֵׁנָה... שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל — the Oral Torah demands great hardship and lost sleep, and its students are 'the people who walked in darkness' who see the great hidden light. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Tanchuma [Noach] 2; correct: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3)*
**Isaiah 9:1** — הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל — the people walking in darkness have seen a great light. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: חֵלֶק ב, סא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב
notes.text: **Zohar II 61b** (Beshalach; Sefaria: Zohar, Beshalach 28:377) — מְזוֹנָא עִלָּאָה יַתִּיר מִכֹּלָּא הוּא מְזוֹנָא דְּחַבְרַיָּיא אִינּוּן דְּמִשְׁתַּדְּלֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא... מֵאֲתָר עִלָּאָה... וְאִקְרֵי חָכְמָה — the highest food is that of the companions who toil in Torah: food of spirit and soul from the place called Wisdom, hence 'wisdom gives life to its possessors'. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Sh'lach 11** (Rav Tzadok) — the same Zohar (II 61b), ranked above the manna, applied to Shabbat: on Shabbat every Jew counts as one who toils in Torah (מִשְׁתַּדְּלֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא), so that the holiness of his eating comes from above. *checked*
**Psalms 104:15** — וְיַיִן יְשַׂמַּח לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ — wine that gladdens the heart of man. *Mafteach: found*
**Proverbs 14:10** — לֵב יוֹדֵעַ מָרַּת נַפְשׁוֹ וּבְשִׂמְחָתוֹ לֹא יִתְעָרַב זָר — the heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy: joy belongs to the heart. *Mafteach: found*
**Proverbs 4:23** — מִכָּל מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים — guard your heart above all, for life flows out of it. He uses the phrase without naming it. *Mafteach: missing*
**Psalms 97:11** — אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה — light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart. *Mafteach: found*

**Ta'anit 15a** — לֹא הַכֹּל לְאוֹרָה וְלֹא הַכֹּל לְשִׂמְחָה; צַדִּיקִים לְאוֹרָה וִישָׁרִים לְשִׂמְחָה — R. Nachman bar Yitzchak: not all receive light and not all receive joy; light is for the righteous and joy for the upright. Rav Tzadok makes the two a ladder: the tzaddik still fights his heart, the upright one has already straightened it. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Tzav 7** (Rav Tzadok) — the same reading of Ta'anit 15a: the tzaddik is a warrior who conquers his inclination and so cannot yet feel joy while his heart is at war; only when the heart becomes straight does joy and rest come. It ties this to Shabbat wine, Megillah 12b and Eruvin 65a (נִכְנַס יַיִן יָצָא סוֹד). *checked*
**Proverbs 13:9** — אוֹר צַדִּיקִים יִשְׂמָח וְנֵר רְשָׁעִים יִדְעָךְ — the light of the righteous rejoices. *Mafteach: found*
**Psalms 149:2** — יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֹשָׂיו בְּנֵי צִיּוֹן יָגִילוּ בְמַלְכָּם — Israel rejoices in its Maker, Zion's children in their King. *Mafteach: found*
**Psalms 97:12** — שִׂמְחוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּה' וְהוֹדוּ לְזֵכֶר קָדְשׁוֹ — rejoice in God, you righteous. *Mafteach: found*
**Isaiah 29:19** — וְיָסְפוּ עֲנָוִים בַּה' שִׂמְחָה — the humble will add joy in God. *Mafteach: found*

**Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Rabbah 3** — עוֹד אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ: אֲנִי יָרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי — King David: I feared out of my joy and rejoiced out of my fear. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 3)*

**Parallels:** **Mei HaShiloach, Vol. II, Berakhot 4a** (Ishbitz–Radzin) — R. Mordechai Yosef cites the same Tanna DeVei Eliyahu: joy and fear, which a person cannot unite by himself, are joined in the heart only by God's help, and whoever succeeds in uniting them is a 'son of the World to Come'. This matches Rav Tzadok's point that true joy is joy in God's sovereignty. *checked*
**Ecclesiastes 2:2** — לִשְׂחוֹק אָמַרְתִּי מְהוֹלָל וּלְשִׂמְחָה מַה זֹּה עֹשָׂה — of laughter I said it is madness, and of joy, what does it accomplish? *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 40a** — רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: גֶּפֶן הָיָה, שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁמֵּבִיא יְלָלָה עַל הָאָדָם אֶלָּא יַיִן — R. Meir: the forbidden tree was a vine, for nothing brings wailing on a person like wine (also Sanhedrin 70a–b). *Mafteach: found*
**Judges 9:13** — הֶחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת תִּירוֹשִׁי הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ אֱלֹהִים וַאֲנָשִׁים — in Yotam's parable the vine speaks of its wine, which cheers God and men. *Mafteach: missing*

**Megillah 12b** — אֲמַר רָבָא: יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת הָיָה, שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין מַתְחִילִין בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּבְדִבְרֵי תִשְׁבָּחוֹת — Rava: the seventh day was Shabbat, when Israel open their eating and drinking with words of Torah and praise, while the nations open theirs with frivolity. *Mafteach: found*
**Esther 1:10** — בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי כְּטוֹב לֵב הַמֶּלֶךְ בַּיָּיִן — on the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine. *Mafteach: found*

**Sifrei Devarim 49** (Ekev, on Deut. 11:22) — דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אוֹמְרִים: רְצוֹנְךָ שֶׁתַּכִּיר מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם? לְמוֹד הַגָּדָה, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ כָּךְ אַתָּה מַכִּיר אֶת הקב"ה וּמִדַּבֵּק בִּדְרָכָיו — if you wish to know the One who spoke and the world came to be, study Aggadah, and through it you will know Him and cleave to His ways. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Sifrei §33 (Re'eh); correct: Sifrei Devarim 49)*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Be'er HaGolah, Well 6 15:81-86** (Machshava) — on Maharal's defence of Aggadah, the notes gather the same Sifrei with Chagigah 14a ('the masters of Aggadah draw a person's heart like water'): Aggadah is divine wisdom, so through it one comes to know God and cleave to Him.
ולכך מתוך האגדה מכיר את הקב"ה, כי אין האגדה אלא "חכמה אלקית"

**Shabbat 87a** — דִּכְתִיב: וַיַּגֵּד מֹשֶׁה — דְּבָרִים שֶׁמּוֹשְׁכִין לִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּאַגָּדָה — Rebbi: 'Moshe told' (וַיַּגֵּד) means words that draw a person's heart, as Aggadah does. *Mafteach: found*
**Exodus 19:9** — וַיַּגֵּד מֹשֶׁה אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָעָם אֶל ה' — Moshe reported the people's words to God; the verse the Gemara expounds. *Mafteach: missing*
**Daniel 7:10** — נְהַר דִּי נוּר נָגֵד וְנָפֵק מִן קֳדָמוֹהִי — a river of fire streamed out before Him. He takes אגדה from the root נגד, 'to draw / flow forth'. *Mafteach: missing*

**Bereishit Rabbah 66:3** — רַבִּי אַחָא אָמַר: יִתֶּן לְךָ וְיִתֶּן לְךָ אֱלָהוּתָא — R. Acha: 'may He give you' means He will give you Godliness itself (and Samson later invokes that blessing). Rav Tzadok reads it as the divine word inside the food. *Mafteach: found*

**Bamidbar Rabbah 22:7** — שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת נִבְרְאוּ בָּעוֹלָם... אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מַתְּנוֹת שָׁמַיִם וּבָאוֹת בְּכֹחַ הַתּוֹרָה, אֲבָל גְּבוּרָתוֹ וְעָשְׁרוֹ שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם — wisdom, strength and wealth count only when they are Heaven's gifts and come through the power of Torah. His wording follows this version exactly. *Mafteach: found*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Matot 5** (Buber, Matot 7) — שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּעוֹלָם, חָכְמָה וּגְבוּרָה וָעֹשֶׁר... בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מַתְּנוֹת שָׁמַיִם — the same teaching; the Buber text also reads וּבָאוֹת בְּכֹחַ הַתּוֹרָה. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Tanchuma, Masei)*

**Zohar I 143b** (Toldot; Sefaria: Zohar, Toldot 19:150) — בְּיַעֲקֹב כְּתִיב וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים, וּבְדָא כְּתִיב יִהְיֶה; בְּיַעֲקֹב כְּתִיב מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ, בְּעֵשָׂו כְּתִיב מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְטַל הַשָּׁמַיִם — R. Shimon: for Jacob it says 'God will give', for Esau only 'will be', and the order of heaven and earth is reversed. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Yisrael Kedoshim 7** (Rav Tzadok) — the bread from the side of the Tree of Life is the מוֹצָא פִי ה' in it, which gives eternal life; its physical side, from the Tree of Knowledge, Jacob separated and handed to Esau. Same distinction, told through the sale of the birthright. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Toldot 7** (Rav Tzadok) — the same Zohar I 143b (וְיִתֶּן לְךָ against יִהְיֶה), adding that Esau's share exists only for Jacob's needs (וְאֶת אָחִיךָ תַּעֲבֹד) and that grain and wine were withheld from him lest the eating harm him. *checked*

**Genesis 27:39** — הִנֵּה מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ יִהְיֶה מוֹשָׁבֶךָ וּמִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם מֵעָל — 'Behold, your dwelling shall be of the earth's richness': a description of where Esau would live, not a gift. *Mafteach: found*

**Exodus 16:25** — וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלֻהוּ הַיּוֹם כִּי שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַה' הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה — eat it today, for today is Shabbat to God; the triple 'today' is the basis for three meals. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Exodus 16:23; correct: Exodus 16:25)*

**Shabbat 117b** — כַּמָּה סְעוּדוֹת חַיָּיב אָדָם לֶאֱכוֹל בַּשַּׁבָּת — שָׁלֹשׁ... וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלוּהוּ הַיּוֹם — three meals on Shabbat, learned from the three 'today's of the verse, one of them counting the evening. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 40a** — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חִטָּה הָיְתָה, שֶׁאֵין הַתִּינוֹק יוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת אַבָּא וְאִמָּא עַד שֶׁיִּטְעוֹם טַעַם דָּגָן — R. Yehudah: the Tree of Knowledge was wheat, for a child cannot say 'abba' and 'imma' until he has tasted grain (also Sanhedrin 70b). For Rav Tzadok, grain means Da'at. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Sulam on Zohar, Yitro 338** (Kabbalah) — on R. Abba's reading of וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם, the dew of Isaac's blessing is the dew that flows from Atika Kadisha into Ze'ir Anpin, through which the dead will rise. This is the 'dew of Atika' Rav Tzadok names as the source of the Oral Torah.
אשר טל הזה יוצא מעתיקא קדישא לזעיר אנפין, הנקרא שמים

**Proverbs 12:19** — שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד וְעַד אַרְגִּיעָה לְשׁוֹן שָׁקֶר — truthful speech stands forever. It closes the link between the third meal, Jacob's attribute of truth, and Aggadah. *Mafteach: found*
